newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL CACHOEIRA DOURADA SALE ATTRACTS 19 FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL CACHOEIRA DOURADA SALE ATTRACTS 19 FIRMS.

text.p: The upcoming privatization of Brazilian Goias state power generator Cachoeira Dourada has attracted the interest of at least 19 Brazilian and foreign firms, a state planning department spokesman said.

A 78.9 percent stake in the 658-megawatt hydroelectric plant is due to be sold off in a closed-envelope auction on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange September 5 at a base price of 543.4 million reais.
The spokesman said the following companies had shown interest in acquiring Cachoeira Dourada.
Interested investors have until August 25 to pre-qualify for the auction, with those companies which pre-qualified to be announced August 29.

Cachoeira Dourada was created in November 1996 when Goias state spun off the generating arm of its power company Centrais Electricas de Goias (Celg), which now only owns a few minor generators and is mainly a power distributor.
The state planning spokesman said Goias state had taken no decision so far whether to privatize Celg as well at a future date.

He said there was no immediate need for the state government to sell Celg because it expected to earn enough from the Cachoeira Dourada sale to finance planned infrastructure projects over the next 12-15 months worth 600 million reais. ($o1.08 reais)
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
